Definition: from G906; a missile, i.e. javelin:--dart.
BiblicalUsage: A dart is the word for a missile, a javelin — and the noun itself never stands alone in the New Testament text. The sounding of the deep in the shipwreck story uses the verb form instead, the heaving of the lead, and the noun is known only from the lexicon, not from a verse of its own. I say so plainly, because a word with no verse should not be given one.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that an honest gap is better than a borrowed verse: this word has no passage of its own, and I will not pretend otherwise.
